body:
Looked at this vs current main (layerwise, `reload_weights`, NCCL/IPC, `sharded_rdt`). I think the restore story is broken.

Rematerializing a live layer and re-running PWAL is the right thing to kill. Checkpoint tensors on the wire and `load_weights` as the router are fine. Stable `data_ptr` is not a commit though. You still have to swap or keep every object the graph can see, and you need the old generation until every rank finishes B.

**Restore vs Constraint 1**

You say `data_ptr` never changes, then the write path is `copy_` or `resize_`+`copy_`. The must-fallback table says Marlin changes `data_ptr` through `resize_`, and PR D-marlin still proposes that resize. On main Marlin does not `resize_` the weight. It assigns the packed result with `x.data = ops.gptq_marlin_repack(...)` and `replace_parameter`. I can't tell which of those the restore path is written against. Same split for DeepGemm (must-fallback *and* PR D-moe).

Layerwise stashes the captured tensors in `kernel_tensors`, points the module at meta, processes a temp, `copy_` back. Captured storage stays put until that last copy. C writes checkpoint layout into the captured storage for the whole receive.

If you've drained and B restores the exact captured shape/stride/dtype/pointer before replay, a same-numel transpose by itself is probably fine. Realloc, B that doesn't put metadata back, aliases still observing the changed layout, graph objects that aren't Parameters, or a fail after START already wrote live storage, are not.

START has already mutated those tensors. If a later NCCL chunk fails, finish throws, or a rank dies, then what? After START mutates live state, a failed RECEIVE or FINISH must not leave the model eligible to serve a partial commit. The previous generation must remain recoverable until every rank completes B successfully. Layerwise at least preserves the old captured storage until each layer's final copy-back, although it is not a model-wide transaction either. C overwrites that storage earlier and therefore makes the failure window larger unless the old generation is saved elsewhere. Drain is not rollback.

**C doesn't put the loader back**

The RFC treats C as "put the param in checkpoint layout so `weight_loader` can stay as-is." After per-tensor FP8 PWAL, `fp8.py` does `weight.t()` then `replace_parameter(layer, "weight", weight.data)` with `prefer_copy` false. That makes a plain `nn.Parameter`, keeps the old loader callable, and drops the `ModelWeightParameter` subclass and old attributes such as `output_dim`; consequently, subclass methods such as `load_qkv_weight` are no longer available. Changing shape in C does not recreate those. `Fp8LinearMethod` is still on `WEIGHT_LOADER_V2_SUPPORTED`, so the bound loader is `weight_loader_v2`, which calls `load_qkv_weight` / `load_column_parallel_weight`. I didn't run every FP8 path. Doesn't change the point: C that only transposes or resizes storage does not recover the Parameter type or the create-time markers.

`output_dim` is also used for two different axes (checkpoint shard vs live write). After a transpose those aren't the same. You still need name routing. The dest of `copy_` does not have to be checkpoint layout.

**The other PRs, and mixed fallback**

#49459 is DIRECT inside layerwise for layout-identical tensors, same first author, still draft / needs-rebase after #49519. #51378 and #53438 are modelwise from the other coauthor. #49789 is the arena for graph-visible stuff that Parameter `copy_` misses. You don't mention those three. #52497 is listed as open; it merged Aug 26.

The RFC doesn't say how these fit together or which one is the plan. Maybe they can live as separate modes. This writeup doesn't define that.

60 selective linears + 1 layerwise MLA is the nasty case and it isn't in the matrix. `initialize_layerwise_reload_for_module` isn't in the tree. Init is still model-wide. Per-module if/else also doesn't handle shared storage (`embed_tokens` / `lm_head`) sitting in two places with different restore vs copy vs fallback. I'd fall back the whole model for that session until alias groups, order, and rollback actually exist.

**These stay even if you drop C-A-B**

Selective A is eager `copy_` with no required-key set. FINISH that rebuilds `W_UK_T` from `kv_b_proj` can mix old and new if a shard, scale, or expert never showed up. You need a generation id, whether sparse updates are allowed, and errors on missing/dup names.

Own storage/alias groups, not modules.

The wrapper quantizes `loaded_weight` then calls `original_loader`. That loader is the TP narrow / `packed_dim` / qkv `shard_id` / expert skip. Some globally aligned blocks can be quantized before sharding and still be correct. You have to show alignment and scale routing per packed/TP loader, not assume every block quant is shard-local. The order that naturally fits today's loaders is to route/select the destination shard first, transform that shard, and then copy its data and scales. That's a new boundary. The loaders don't expose it cleanly today.

**PR A**

`supports_selective_reload` on the method class can't encode `Fp8LinearMethod`. DeepGemm vs Triton vs CUTLASS is picked at runtime. Block FP8 method PWAL skips the transpose then always calls `self.fp8_linear.process_weights_after_loading`. Whether block FP8 can `copy_` depends on the kernel.

Unquantized is not the same as layout-identical. CPU can drop the weight. XPU rewrites layout. AITER / FlashInfer / TRTLLM MoE shuffle or swap w13 to w31 on first PWAL. `default_weight_loader` only checks size. If PR A returns True for unquantized, those backends silently corrupt.

Not just Parameters. `W_UK_T_dcp_qrep` (assigned from `all_gather`), TRT-LLM `_g1_alphas` on the experts object, B12x wrapper workspaces, Marlin workspace. #49789 is the attempt to register that stuff. If you only walk `QuantizeMethodBase` you also miss MLA state on the attention module. Banning `replace_parameter` fights `prefer_copy=True`.

`sharded_rdt` (#43375) is another checkpoint-format engine. `rdt-quant` thread runs PWAL + copy-back, then `info.reset()` on completed layers so finalize only does leftovers (attention). `finish` has to `drain_pending()` first. When PR A says three engines / RDT quant-thread, this is what it's talking about.

75/88 no-ops is not a reason to skip finish. A lot of those PWALs just call a pack kernel.

veRL / OpenRLHF / NeMo-RL send BF16. That's the trainer, not the engine being BF16. If the engine is FP8 the first PRs are not most of the work. H/I wrapping `weight_loader` at `create_weights` changes cold start.

In-order extra VRAM is one layer, not 2x the model. Pack is not compile. If prod DeepSeek-V3 is DeepGemm, PR B skipping DeepGemm doesn't move peak mem.

I'd rebase #49459 now that #49519 is in and see if it's still the right layout-identical path, before adding `selective.py` or engine if/else. If you still want reverse-transform, put it in the current start/finish, only for methods that `copy_` into existing storage, and stage into a temp instead of mutating the captured tensor. I'd try per-tensor FP8 first. It still has to restore Parameter metadata, not just shape. Leave Marlin and DeepGemm on layerwise until that actually works. Fall back the whole session. start/finish also has to handle `sharded_rdt`'s quant thread and `drain_pending()`, not just NCCL/IPC. Don't hook online quant into `create_weights` in this work.

Separate from this RFC: `reload_weights` only resets encoder/mm cache. `finish_weight_update` never calls `reload_weights`. Prefix extra keys are LoRA, MM, `cache_salt`, prompt embeds. No `weight_version`. Shared system prompt can hit KV from the old weights after an update. Already true today.

I am preparing a separate **draft for architectural comparison** from `new-TonyWang:hapi-review-weight-reload-tracker` (implementation head `ba1e6ebf17`).

Duplicate-work checks included the comments on this RFC and #48312, open PRs referencing both issues, and open reload PRs. This overlaps the problem space of #55595, #51378, #53438, #50564, and #49789, but changes the implementation contract:

- Ordinary layers record sharding/arrival slots during actual cold loading; routed experts generate the expected slots from the current expert mapping each reload round. No copy-count/range interception or dummy-load probing.
- Backend policies separate cold-only PWAL installation from repeatable FP8 conversion. A layer finishes as soon as its slots and dependencies complete, then releases staging, rather than waiting for modelwise PWAL/publication.
- Policies prepare writable checkpoint-layout views over compatible runtime storage, otherwise stage. Optional checkpoint preservation disables this reuse. This restores a loading layout, not old checkpoint values, and does not resize/rebind the serving tensor.
- The NCCL/IPC path is opt-in; default layerwise behavior remains unchanged.

Compared with #55595, the central change is the trace/state/processing-plan lifecycle and multi-backend loading-layout reuse, not another standalone CUTLASS fix. Compared with #51378/#53438, this is deliberately per-layer and non-transactional. It is not a general ReloadArena replacement (#49789) or the dummy manifest probe in #50564.

Inference must be drained and expert placement fixed during a round. Partial updates, concurrent EPLB movement, rollback, and model-wide atomic publication are not supported. Failure after runtime writes is terminal for serving. Latest focused H200 regression: 249 passed, 2 skipped; final-head full-model evaluation and native platform coverage remain incomplete.

The draft is intended to make these alternatives reviewable and reconcile the overlapping proposals before merge, not to merge competing reload infrastructures independently. AI assistance was used; human line-by-line review and test reproduction remain required.

### Follow-ups
- **F2** Rest of the update-boundary checks: MTP/draft completeness at the boundary instead of per call (#49090); refuse to serve while a direct update is pending (#64418 §8).
- **F4** Online quantization leftovers: `fp8_per_block` MoE crashes on the first request (also on main); online MoE with EPLB is refused because staged quant configs keep temporary scales.
- **F6** Muse Spark MegaMoE: `finalize_weights` runs once and drops or rebinds the expert parameters; transform in place and refill the hybrid decode constants.
- **F7** Remove layerwise reload: needs 22, `draft_lm_head_quantization` and LoRA in direct mode, torchao and expert substitution off layerwise; then #64418 X1–X4.
- **F8** Direct reload as the default: needs 10 and 17 (in progress: the default-switch PR, which also moves every direct-mode refusal from startup to reload time); 12 and 18 are not prerequisites (2026-11-17).
- **F9** Per-family refit CI steps keyed on each family's files, on reduced synthetic checkpoints; a family is marked by 12 together with its step.
- **F11** Level-2 sleep. RL colocates training, so every update runs `sleep(level=2)` → `wake_up(["weights"])` → update → `wake_up(["kv_cache"])`. Level 2 discards the weights pool, so state there that is not a checkpoint tensor and that PWAL does not rewrite is lost. The validations in Families ran without sleep mode.
  - Non-parameter state in the weights pool (permutation indices, GEMM-RS/AR peer pointer tables, and the same pattern elsewhere): 24 discards only parameters at level 2 instead of fixing sites one by one. Over NCCL, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash goes 0.90 → 0.0 on main and holds on this PR in 3 runs, with the fixed-token oracle unchanged. Beam NVFP4 hangs after the first level-2 update on main and holds 0.945 on this PR. Kimi-K3 placeholder weights stop crashing with GEMM-AR on. Host backup grows about 2%. XPU isn't tested yet. It supersedes the site fixes in #60009, #62634 and #64922.
  - MoE expert padding is undefined after a wake: 3 zero-fills it at begin.
  - Specialized decode paths are off under sleep mode (DeepSeek-V4.1 NVIDIA, Kimi-K3 NVIDIA, Muse Spark NVIDIA, MiniMax-M3 AMD): output is correct but rollouts are slower. Decide between supporting sleep and listing it as a limitation.
  - The refit test (9) runs a level-2 sleep/wake around each update; families are revalidated with sleep mode on (`tools/state_transition_verifier` does this by default).

### Limitations
- NVFP4 MegaMoE (MiniMax-M3) passes the L2 activation scale as a host float, so CUDA graphs keep the cold-start value when an update changes `w2_input_scale`.
- FULL-graph decode on kernels that take only host-float KV scales (FlashInfer FA2 decode pre-SM100, ROCm AITER asm (hao-aaron/vllm#12)) keeps the startup scales after a KV-scale update; to be refused by 12 ([note](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/66002#issuecomment-6749310799)).
- A model tied at cold start (config tie, or re-tied because the checkpoint's `lm_head` equals the embeddings) can't be untied by an update: direct reload drops a differing `lm_head`, layerwise overwrites the input embeddings with it.
- At TP>1 a refused update leaves stale RPC replies and the engine dies on the next request (#60401).
- Layerwise reload: objects PWAL builds keep pointing at the temporary parameters (FP8 MoE `moe_quant_config` scales, CuteDSL NVFP4 `localized_shards`); outputs correct, memory duplicated. Goes away with F7.
- gpt-oss full-checkpoint loaders assume an even expert-parallel split; uneven EP mis-slices experts (hao-aaron/vllm#13).
- 26 does not load AMD Quark GLM-5.3-Flash (`amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4`, block-FP8 MLA with Quark `weight_scale`), which main loads; deferred to a follow-up. With 26, a BF16 `wk`/MLA update still counts the retired FP8 scale, so layerwise reload buffers the layer and sharded RDT refuses it.

### Notes
- Direct-mode assumptions: every update resends every required tensor (enforced by 17); breaking layerwise reload is acceptable.
- Weight names: hmellor [asks](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54477#issuecomment-6607872192) whether trainers should send module names instead of checkpoint names once #60666 (apply Transformers v5 checkpoint renamings at load) lands. Worth standardizing on; 17 checks parameters, not names, so it works with either.
- #48972 moves every model's `load_weights` onto `AutoWeightsLoader`. Most split-update bugs here were in hand-written loops (Molmo, GLM5-next, gpt-oss, MiMo), so reload fixes should follow that direction rather than add per-model loader code.
- Moved to the load plan (#64418): batched per-expert loading (L1); static FP8 MoE `input_scale` slot and the compressed-tensors check (L4); PR 6's FP8-in-BF16 rows (L7); sharded RDT on DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM5-next (E1).

On the Families table in the [tracker](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54477#issuecomment-6450991360): PR 6 is needed only by the flagships whose `load_weights` combines several checkpoint tensors. Grepping `stash_weight_part` / `_try_load_fp8_indexer_wk` callers at `98c622daf4`:

| Family | Code | Combined in `load_weights` |
|---|---|---|
| Hy4 | `hy_v4/{nvidia,amd}/model.py`, `hy_v4/nvidia/mtp.py` | indexer `wk` FP8 weight + scale → BF16 |
| dots3 | `dots3_note/nvidia/model.py` | indexer `wk` FP8 weight + scale → BF16 |
| GLM-5.3 | `glm5next/common/{model,mtp}.py` (or `deepseek_v32` for `GlmMoeDsa`) | indexer `wk`; on glm5next also the FP8 MLA projections |
| MiMo-V2.6 | `mimo_v2.py`, `mimo_v2_mtp.py` | fused FP8 qkv: dequant, reorder, requant |

Ling-3, Step-5, Kimi-K3, Beam and Gemma-4 do not combine tensors in `load_weights`, so their rows should read `1, 2, 4` and `1, 2, 4, 5`. Suggest splitting those two rows.

Correction to the comment above: the public HY-V4 and dots3 checkpoints store the indexer `wk` in BF16, so `_try_load_fp8_indexer_wk` never triggers for them and they do not need PR 6 in practice. With today's checkpoints PR 6 matters for GLM-5.3 (indexer `wk`, and the FP8 MLA projections on glm5next) and MiMo-V2.6 (fused FP8 qkv); HY-V4 and dots3 need it only for an FP8-`wk` checkpoint.

Hi @hao-aaron @aoshen02, I'd like to help with F17: refusing generation while a direct reload is pending.

My proposed scope is an execution guard plus focused regressions for pending updates, transfer/post-load failures, and recovery after a subsequent successful full update, coordinating target/draft handling with the current worker lifecycle.

Is someone already handling F17, or can I take this slice?

Hey! We'd love another set of eyes on this RFC related PR. If you leave constructive feedback that gets merged in, we'll gladly add you as a co-author!

@aoshen02 @hao-aaron I found a reproducible Muse DSpark loading regression while reviewing the RFC-related loader changes on main `5d55ef159`.

`MuseSparkDSparkModel` initializes `nn.Module` directly and does not create DFlash's optional `_context_kv_proj`. The inherited `DFlashQwen3Model.load_weights` now reads it unconditionally (added in #64357). A minimal single-call load with `lm_head.weight`, `d2t`, and valid `fc.weight` entries fails with:

```text
AttributeError: 'MuseSparkDSparkModel' object has no attribute '_context_kv_proj'
```

## Weight-update speed (direct reload + load plan, packed NCCL, GB200)

Updates go trainer GPU → inference GPU over NCCL; nothing is read from disk, so loader speedups such as safetensors prefetch help cold start only. An update costs three things: the broadcast, the copies into the parameters, and rerunning post-load processing. The PRs below cut them; the flagships now update in 0.6–1.7 s, against 7.5–12 s on main.

**Setup.** A GPU-resident sender on separate GB200 nodes (4 broadcasting ranks per node) feeds vLLM at TP4, or TP8×PP2 across nodes for the largest models. Each update runs level-2 sleep → wake weights → start → broadcasts → finish → wake KV. The time is `start_weight_update` → `finish_weight_update`, steady state. Correctness is GSM8K before vs after four updates from a real start.

### How close to the limit

- A 1 GiB NCCL broadcast across two GB200 nodes peaks at ~650 GB/s. Protocols, channels and buffer sizes change it by ≤4%; Tree and NVLS do not support broadcast.
- Every receiver gets every byte, so the wire floor is ~0.24 s for DSv4-Flash (156 GB), ~0.46 s for DSv4.1 (300 GB) and ~1.2 s for Kimi-K3 (~780 GB per stage). We are at 1.4–2.6× that floor.
- The rest is copies into the parameters (~40% on top of receiving) and post-load processing at finish (~0.18 s on DSv4.1).
- Tried, ≤3% each:
  - overlapping post-load processing with later turns;
  - more receive buffers;
  - high-priority NCCL streams;
  - a single RPC for all turns.
